match.reason: The closest bank point, Bearings and elevation, covers clockwise-from-north bearings together with angles of elevation and depression, so it is broader and does not teach compass bearings like S45°E, which makes it not the same idea.

draft.title: True and compass bearings
card: a three-figure angle measured clockwise from north, such as 045°T or 135°T. North is 000°T, east is 090°T, south is 180°T and west is 270°T.
an angle from north or south turned towards east or west, such as S45°E. Start facing south, then turn 45° towards east.
To convert: N θ E = θ. S θ E = 180 − θ. S θ W = 180 + θ. N θ W = 360 − θ.
Example: S30°W is 30° past south towards west, so the true bearing is 180 + 30 = 210°T.
draft.remember: True bearings turn clockwise from north. Compass bearings turn from north or south.

a.q: What is the true bearing of N40°W?
a.why: N40°W is 40° from north towards west, which is 40° short of a full turn: 360 − 40 = 320°T. 040°T is wrong because that is N40°E, towards east.

b.q: A ship leaves port on a true bearing of 250°T. What is its compass bearing?
b.why: 250° lies between south (180°) and west (270°). It is 250 − 180 = 70° past south towards west, so S70°W. S20°W is wrong because it is 20° past south, which is 200°T.
b.clue: 250° is between south at 180° and west at 270°.
